observation.visible_scene: A showroom-style suspended ceiling made of a metal grid with square panels, densely populated by several operating ceiling fans. The most prominent is a center-top fan with four curved orange/amber blades and a bright white frosted light dome. Around it are: a chrome-bodied fan with transparent blades on the left; a red-bladed fan with a white light dome below center; a white-bladed fan with a small light and, beside it, a dark wooden-bladed fan with a warm amber light on the right; a small white fan lower-center; a brown-bladed fan intruding at the top-right edge; and a row of lit bulbs along the bottom-left. The lights on the fans remain steadily illuminated.
visible_changes: The orange central fan's blades rotate continuously throughout the excerpt, appearing as motion-blurred arcs whose angular positions shift from frame to frame; the rotation is already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last, with no start or stop visible.
The red-bladed fan, the white-bladed fan, the wooden-bladed fan, and the top-right brown fan likewise keep spinning continuously, their blades blurred and repositioning across successive frames.
The chrome fan on the left shows faint blade movement consistent with rotation, though its transparent blades make the motion hard to track.
The ceiling grid, panel seams, and all glowing light fixtures stay fixed in the same image positions across every frame, indicating a stationary camera rather than camera motion.
No object enters or leaves the scene; the set of fans and lights is constant, with only the blades' rotational orientation changing.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fan speed settings, switch states, or any control actions that produced the rotation are not shown.
What happened before the first frame or after the last frame (e.g., fans starting/stopping, people, store activity) is unknown.
The exact rotational direction and angular speed of each fan cannot be determined from these sampled frames.
uncertain_details: Whether the left chrome fan is actually spinning or merely showing reflections is ambiguous due to its clear blades.
The precise rotation direction (clockwise vs counter-clockwise) of each fan is not reliably inferable from the blur patterns.
Minor differences in blade blur between frames could partly reflect sampling timing rather than a change in speed; the rotation appears steady but exact uniformity is uncertain.
